caption: The drawing features a single object, a powder horn, displayed horizontally on a plain, off-white background. The powder horn is curved and tapers from a broader, rounded base on the right to a narrower, pointed tip on the left. The horn itself is colored in shades of tan, ivory, and brown, with distinct darker striping and shading following the natural texture of the horn. The base is capped with a circular, slightly domed wooden or metal end, attached with a series of small fasteners, and has a small loop or ring for carrying. The narrower tip is also fitted with a dark brown collar, possibly made of leather or wood. Engraved letters on the side of the horn are visible and read, "J.A. Dial," followed by "Cabell County," "Virginia May 4th 1861." The lines and shading of the drawing are rendered in a realistic style, capturing the texture and material qualities of the horn. There are faint lines marking the border of the illustration and some small, handwritten notations near the bottom edge of the paper.
title: Powder Horn
